Quote.body: You have power over your mind - not outside events.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: What stands in the way becomes the way.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: When you arise in the morning, think of what a precious privilege it is to be alive.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Very little is needed to make a happy life.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Look well into thyself; there is a source of strength which will always spring up.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: What is not good for the swarm is not good for the bee.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Everything we hear is an opinion, not a fact.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: It's not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: No man is free who is not master of himself.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: We have two ears and one mouth so that we can listen twice as much as we speak.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: No great thing is created suddenly.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: If anyone tells you that a certain person speaks ill of you, do not make excuses.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Only the educated are free.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Freedom is the only worthy goal in life.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: No one can make you feel inferior without your consent.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
Quote.author: Seneca
Quote.attribution: On the Shortness of Life (c. 49 CE) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Seneca_the_Younger

Quote.body: It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste much of it.
Quote.author: Seneca
Quote.attribution: On the Shortness of Life (c. 49 CE) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Seneca_the_Younger

Quote.body: Associate with people who are likely to improve you.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Difficulties show what men are.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: How long are you going to wait before you demand the best for yourself?
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: No person has the power to have everything they want, but in their power is not to want what they do not have.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Receive without pride, let go without attachment.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Nowhere can man find a quieter or more untroubled retreat than in his own soul.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is not due to the thing itself.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: No one can lose either the past or the future - how could anyone be deprived of what he does not possess?
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Reject your sense of injury and the injury itself disappears.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Objective judgment, now, at this very moment. Unselfish action, now.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: If someone is able to show me that what I think or do is not right, I will happily change.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: It is impossible for a man to learn what he thinks he already knows.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Freedom is secured not by the fulfilling of desires, but by the removal of desire.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Circumstances do not make the man, they only reveal him to himself.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: If you seek tranquility, do less.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: As long as you live, keep learning how to live.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for kindness.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: He who fears death will never do anything worthy of a living man.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: There is no easy way from the earth to the stars.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Every new beginning comes from some other beginning's end.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Compassion is the basis of morality.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer

Quote.body: Talent hits a target no one else can hit; genius hits a target no one else can see.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer

Quote.body: Every man takes the limits of his own field of vision for the limits of the world.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer

Quote.body: Mostly it is loss which teaches us about the worth of things.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer

Quote.body: A man can do what he wants, but not want what he wants.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
Quote.attribution: On the Freedom of the Will (1839) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Arthur_Schopenhauer

Quote.body: Life swings like a pendulum backward and forward between pain and boredom. The two enemies of human happiness are pain and boredom.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
Quote.attribution: Composite of two Schopenhauer lines: Studies in Pessimism themes; Personality; or, What a Man Is | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Arthur_Schopenhauer

Quote.body: Never combat any man's opinion; for though you reached the age of Methuselah, you would never have done setting him right upon all the absurd things that he believes.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
Quote.attribution: Counsels and Maxims, Ch. III, § 38 (trans. T. Bailey Saunders) | https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Counsels_and_Maxims/Chapter_III

Quote.body: We forfeit three-fourths of ourselves in order to be like other people.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
Quote.attribution: Aphorisms on the Wisdom of Life | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Arthur_Schopenhauer

Quote.body: Money is human happiness in the abstract.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer
Quote.attribution: Aphorisms on the Wisdom of Life | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Arthur_Schopenhauer

Quote.body: Buying books would be a good thing if one could also buy the time to read them.
Quote.author: Arthur Schopenhauer

Quote.body: Objective judgment, now, at this very moment.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Confine yourself to the present.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Loss is nothing else but change, and change is Nature's delight.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Never let the future disturb you. You will meet it, if you have to, with the same weapons of reason which today arm you against the present.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: The art of living is more like wrestling than dancing.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: External things are not the problem. It is your assessment of them.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: You always own the option of having no opinion.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Be tolerant with others and strict with yourself.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: The object of life is not to be on the side of the majority.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Receive wealth or prosperity without arrogance, and be ready to let it go.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: A blazing fire makes flame and brightness out of everything that is thrown into it.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Dig within. Within is the wellspring of good.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: The universe is change; our life is what our thoughts make it.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Perfection of character is this: to live each day as if it were your last.
Quote.author: Marcus Aurelius

Quote.body: Some things are within our power, while others are not.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of them.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Do not explain your philosophy. Embody it.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Seek not for events to happen as you wish, but wish them to happen as they do happen.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: If evil be said of you and it be true, correct yourself; if it is a lie, laugh at it.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Know, first, who you are, and then adorn yourself accordingly.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: It is not death or pain that is to be dreaded, but the fear of pain or death.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: If you want to improve, be content to be thought foolish and stupid.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Who then is invincible? The one who cannot be upset by anything outside reasoned choice.
Quote.author: Epictetus

Quote.body: Lead me, Zeus, and thou, O Destiny.
Quote.author: Cleanthes

Quote.body: He suffers more than necessary, who suffers before it is necessary.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: A gem cannot be polished without friction, nor a man perfected without trials.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: We become wiser by adversity.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Fire is the test of gold; adversity, of strong men.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: No man was ever wise by chance.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: The bravest sight in the world is to see a great man struggling against adversity.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: It is a rough road that leads to the heights of greatness.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Time discovers truth.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: He is most powerful who has himself in his own power.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Leisure without study is death.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Fate leads the willing and drags along the reluctant.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: To bear trials with a calm mind robs misfortune of its strength and burden.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: Everywhere means nowhere. When a person spends all his time in foreign travel, he ends by having many acquaintances, but no friends.
Quote.author: Seneca

Quote.body: He who is brave is free.
Quote.author: Seneca
